detection_classes.independent_review: Found by a reviewer outside the session that wrote the artifact: the independent review of 2026-08-06, or the clinical reviewers of 2026-08-23.
detection_classes.internal_review: Found by a session's own review, sweep, naming review, pre-validation audit, or while writing something else.
detection_classes.automated_gate: Found by a check that failed: the release gate refusing to write, or a test going red.
detection_classes.use: Found by someone operating the application rather than reviewing it.

hand_count.label: Counted quantities maintained by hand
hand_count.definition: A headline figure, table cell or summary field states a count of artifacts (requirements, hazards, tests, documents, signatures, rows) that a person typed and nobody re-measured when the artifacts changed. The fact is countable from the tree; the document carries a stale copy of the count.

prose_count.label: Unguarded prose counts
prose_count.definition: A measured quantity embedded in running prose rather than in a field a generator owns — a sentence that says how many of something there are. The number was right when written and nothing re-reads the sentence.

two_writers.label: Two writers for one fact
two_writers.definition: Two artifacts, or two tools, each hold their own copy of the same fact, and one was updated without the other — a restated register, a duplicated total, a display name kept in two files, a condition implemented twice.

unswept_closure.label: Closure not swept
unswept_closure.definition: Something was closed, withdrawn, added or changed, and the change was recorded where it was made but not in the companion artifacts that also speak about it — a hazard closed in one document and open in another, a profile withdrawn from the catalogue but still listed in a guide, a dependency vendored without its notice.

capability_claim.label: Capability claims outliving code
capability_claim.definition: Live text states that the software lacks a capability, has a limit, or delivers something a particular way, after the code gained the capability, lost the limit, or changed the mechanism. The rule stated may still be right; the stated reason or mechanism has become false.

stale_description.label: Documentation describing software that does not ship
stale_description.definition: Operator-facing or design documentation — SOPs, validation scripts, architecture descriptions, user guides, help pages — describes behaviour, a key layout, a file, a storage location or a control that no longer ships or never shipped. The text was written from memory of the product, or from an earlier version of it, and never re-checked against the screen or the tree.

copied_text.label: Text copied into a context where its facts are false
copied_text.definition: Provenance notes, rationale, basis statements or guidance copied from one profile, document or section into another whose facts differ, so the copy asserts a standard, a target or an instruction that does not apply where it now sits.

traceability.label: Traceability identifiers that point at nothing
traceability.definition: A traceability document cites verification identifiers that no test implements, a test plan numbers cases that exist in no test file, or tests exist that no identifier can cite — the matrix manufactures the appearance of coverage.

test_claim.label: A test claims more than it verifies
test_claim.definition: A test's name, a validation helper, or a verification claim asserts coverage the assertions do not provide: dead instrumentation, a race that reports a false absence, a designed element whose absence no test could see because the tests constructed the input by hand.

version_split.label: Version advanced in one place
version_split.definition: A version identifier — product version, cache key, profile version stamp, document header version — was advanced in one place and not in the others that must agree with it, so two artifacts describe different releases as current.

evidence_provenance.label: Evidence without provenance
evidence_provenance.definition: Test evidence was recorded without the identity of what it measured — no commit hash, no tree state, a command that was not the one run — so a result exists that cannot be reproduced or tied to a released state.

original_defect.label: Original defect, not drift
original_defect.definition: A defect present from the moment it was written rather than a claim that stopped being true: an unobtainable citation carried as support, a validation rule that never checked what it needed to, a default-filling branch that conflated absent with wrong. Recorded in the log because the same machinery now prevents its recurrence.
